title: Holding a Stand-Alone Drug Plan Alongside a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan
content:
A member enrolled in a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan that includes Part D prescription drug coverage may not at the same time hold a stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan.

**Condition of record.** No stand-alone Part D enrollment for the same member is in force on the day the new Medicare Advantage coverage begins, unless the plan being elected is one that carries no Part D coverage. The member's Stand-Alone Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plans enrollment records are the authority, tested before the election is recorded and matched on the member reference; a stand-alone enrollment counts as out of force where it stands disenrolled, terminated for non-payment, or cancelled before it ever took effect.

### Where a stand-alone drug plan is in force

Where a stand-alone drug plan is in force and the elected plan includes Part D, accepting the Medicare Advantage election ends the stand-alone drug plan on the day before the new coverage begins, and the member is told this before the election is recorded.

### Electing the plan that carries no Part D coverage

A member electing the plan that carries no Part D coverage keeps their stand-alone drug plan, and the plan checks that they hold one before recording the election, because a Medicare Advantage member with no drug coverage pays the full price at the pharmacy and may later owe a late enrollment penalty.

### Special Needs Plans

A Special Needs Plan enrollment and an ordinary Medicare Advantage enrollment are mutually exclusive in the same way, and a member who would qualify for a Special Needs Plan is told what they would gain and lose before either election is recorded.
